featured_reviews.review_text:
Vikhroli Social – A Hidden Gem for the Modern Corporate Crowd

Vikhroli Social is truly a hidden gem—an effortlessly modern resto-bar that strikes the perfect balance between quirk and comfort. The moment you walk in, you’re greeted with an energetic yet relaxed vibe, paired with a cleverly curated menu that offers a playful twist on classic favourites. Whether you're in the mood for comfort bites or experimental flavours, their quirky selections won’t disappoint.

One of the standout features is their beautiful rooftop restaurant. It’s an absolute delight during the winter months, offering cosy seating options suitable for every group size—from intimate conversations to larger corporate gatherings. The ambience, paired with great music, sets the tone for unwinding after a long workday.

The service is impeccable, with a team that’s both attentive and welcoming. Their focus on creating an experience tailored for the modern corporate age group is clearly reflected in both the menu and the overall vibe.

I would highly recommend Vikhroli Social to all working professionals in and around the area. Whether you're looking to de-stress, catch up with colleagues, or simply enjoy a lively atmosphere, this is the perfect spot to relax, connect, and elevate your post-work moments.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Vikhroli Social – Elevated Experience with a Spacious Rooftop

I recently visited Vikhroli Social with my office colleagues, and it turned out to be a better experience than my previous visits. The key improvement was their expanded rooftop space. Earlier, the rooftop was more like a small balcony, but now it’s a huge, open, and spacious area. If you prefer a quieter atmosphere without loud music, the rooftop is definitely the best spot. It offers ample space and a relaxed vibe, although the bench table seating felt a bit too compact and could have been more comfortable.

We were a group of four and ordered a variety of dishes. The Veg Platter was average — nothing exceptional, but decent. The Munchao Soup, on the other hand, was quite good with a rich and flavorful broth. We also tried Fish and Chips, which were good but could have been seasoned better. The fish options were quite limited, which was a bit disappointing. However, the corn starter was a pleasant surprise — crispy, well-seasoned, and delicious.

The highlight of the evening was the Wings Platter, which came with four different types of wings. Each preparation had a distinct flavor profile — some spicy, some sweet with BBQ sauce — and every single one tasted amazing. The variety and quality of the wings truly stood out.

Overall, it was a great experience, especially because of the improved rooftop setup. The spacious and relaxed atmosphere, combined with good food and service, made it a memorable evening. If you’re visiting Vikhroli Social, the rooftop is definitely the place to be!

Our inaugural visit to Lake View Café was, regrettably, underwhelming despite its promising premise.

The buffet boasted an impressively expansive spread, encompassing Southeast Asian, Indian, and continental cuisines, reflecting commendable variety and ambition. However, the execution fell short of expectation, with the offerings lacking any discernible “wow” factor.

A particularly notable drawback was the quality of the chicken across several dishes, which appeared less than fresh and was consistently tough, detracting significantly from the dining experience. Even relatively straightforward preparations, such as the pasta, required multiple iterations before reaching an acceptable standard—an avoidable lapse in a setting of this calibre.

Service, too, proved to be disappointingly pedestrian, falling well below the benchmark set by establishments such as JW Marriott Mumbai and Taj Mahal Palace.

In sum, while the breadth of the spread is undeniably impressive, the inconsistency in execution and lacklustre service rendered the experience far from memorable.

In starters, the katsu was crisp and clean, no unnecessary frills, just a really satisfying crunch. For mains, the katsu curry with rice was the sort of dish that makes the entire table go silent while everyone takes their first bite.

The drinks were equally enjoyable. Whether you go for a cocktail or a mocktail, pairing one with the food just completes the whole meal.

The restaurant itself has a very calming vibe. Stone walls, warm wooden elements, and rustic touches give it a relaxed, cosy feel. It’s a quiet escape from the usual bustle and a really pleasant place to unwind over good food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a reservation for 8 people at around 9:30 p.m. on Sunday, but we reached the place around 10 p.m. and there were no tables ready for us. We still had to wait around 10–12 minutes before getting seated near the bar.

The place feels more like a casual hangout spot than a proper family dining restaurant. It’s crowded, music is loud, and lighting is quite dim for dinner, so it doesn’t really suit a calm family meal. Service was also slow due to the rush and limited staff.

Food was mixed — spicy garlic chicken was decent, chicken popcorn was actually good, and the fries were really good. Chicken tenders were average, not very crispy or flavorful. The edamame truffle fried rice was very disappointing and tasted like plain rice with minimal seasoning and very little chicken. The garlic noodles were also decent and didn't really look well tossed.

Hygiene was overall okay, and the toilets were clean enough, but there were mosquitoes present. The interior and exterior also don’t give a premium feel — it looks like a normal casual restaurant rather than anything upscale.

Overall, better suited for casual hangouts or quick bites, not a proper family dinner experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Ruined Evening – Terrible Service & Absolute Lack of Basic Etiquette
​Rating: 1/5 stars
​We had an incredibly frustrating experience at Pop Tate's. While the food was okay, the service was outright appalling and completely ruined our evening.
​We arrived when the restaurant was busy, but even after it emptied out, we ended up sitting there for almost three hours due to pure negligence.
​The Food and the Missing Ingredients:
We ordered the jalapeno cheese balls, but they were served completely missing the jalapeno. When we pointed this out, the server offered to replace it with an avocado alternative... which never even arrived.
​The 1-Hour Delay & Lazy Excuses:
I had to follow up with our server three times about our order. After waiting for over an hour, the server's explanation was that the KOT (Kitchen Order Ticket) hadn't printed in the kitchen. What makes this unacceptable is that the server lacked the basic courtesy to check on the delay or inform us beforehand. I eventually had to ask a completely different server just to find out what was happening, and nobody seemed to have a clue. This is exceptionally poor etiquette from the service team.
​Frustrating "Apology":
At the end of the night, the head server came over with a complimentary pastry to apologize. We politely declined, explaining that the team had already ruined our evening and that they needed to train their staff to pay attention to tables and anticipate guest needs. Instead of listening, the server didn't even apologize verbally and simply brought the pastry again after we had already denied it. This just added to our frustration.
​Final Verdict:
Throughout the night, the servers were completely preoccupied chit-chatting with each other instead of managing their tables. I highlighted this directly to the head server. This branch desperately needs strong, strict supervision and heavy retraining for its staff. I sincerely hope management takes this seriously and improves in the near future, but as of now, I cannot recommend this place.

Things we tried-
1) Korean ramen- 4/5- it’s good but tasted similar to Nissin instant ramen
2) chicken teriyaki gimbap- 4/5- good quantity had 10 big pieces, it was satisfying and flavourful
3) cheese gimbap- 5/5- good quantity with 10 pieces, the flavour was top notch better than the chicken one honestly. Creamy filling. It was a good vegetarian option
4) rabokki- 3.5/5- it is basically a mix of noodles + taekbokki. While the taekbokki texture and flavour was great the gochujang sauce felt a bit sweet to me but if you enjoy gochujang flavour you’ll love it.
5) SPICY SAMGYEOPSAL BELGIUM PORK BELLY- 3/5- it was fine, generic, a bit Chinese flavoured, the meat was well cooked and slightly chewy. I had expected it to be in bbq grill style but it was more like a saucy tossed meat.
6) mochi icecream- 4/5- I loved the red bean paste that they served with the ice cream it was an absolutely new taste to me and I loved it as a combination with mochi ice cream <3

Honest Review!
Malvan Samudra is one of the oldest restaurants in Vikhroli (West) specially known for its authentic sea food and Indian food. It's taste was great especially it's sea food. Good Ambiance and you can visit here with family and friends. They serve Malvan cuisine as well as chinese and others. The specialty is Bombil chilly. I also ordered bheja fry. It was awesome. Eat Fresh Stay Healthy ❤️

You get the same thing in Misal, just with added farsan, and that too in a smaller quantity. I’d recommend only the Vada Pav from here. it’s good, no doubt. But this place is definitely not for Misal or Usal. The Usal tasted just okay as well.

featured_reviews.name: Lav Agrawal
featured_reviews.review_text: Lives up to the hype.. The vada pav was quite tasty... Served with sengdana chutney and finely chopped onions.. It is a quick go to snack.. Worth trying..

featured_reviews.name: Jasmeen Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
Came across bhau Vada pav when I went to Ghatkopar West near railway station I saw a long queue must be 30 people in line for vada pav so I thought let's check out the vada pav.bought 3 took home because it was very crowded and I thought since I got it packed will go home and have it. I must say the vadapav has distinguished taste. And the bread I mean the pav is huge if you have one Vadapav you will skip your lunch.
I have had best of vada pav in Mumbai and according to me this one is 7/10
Some might like it and some will pass it.
If I feel like having Vada pav I will not travel from Ghatkopar east to west because we got one good vada pav vendor here.

featured_reviews.name: Zeeshan Sayyed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bhau Vada Pav is a must-visit for every street food lover in town!
The pav is soft and fresh, and the vada is perfectly crispy on the outside and full of flavor inside. What makes it stand out is the generous layer of chutney and finely chopped onions with a spicy kick absolutely mouthwatering!

Served hot in a foil wrap, it’s perfect for a quick bite. The hygiene is well maintained, and service is super quick. Great taste at a very affordable price!

featured_reviews.name: Sarvesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Vada Pav paired with the dry garlic chutney is a speciality, both in terms of quality as well as in quantity. Having multiple outlets across Mumbai, the food here is quite affordable for the common public. Best time to visit is mainly during non-peak hours, if one wants to avoid long queues and waiting times. Unfortunately,
they don't accept online payments. Cleanliness and hygiene is maintained regularly. Conveniently located just outside the railway station, the place is easily accessible and reachable.

featured_reviews.name: V K
featured_reviews.review_text: Why does everything go wrong once a food joint has earned name and fame. Pathetic experience today, visiting after 2 yrs. The pao was stale and crumby, the vada coating was full of oil & original lasun&chilli pwd sukha chutney was replaced with oily besan fried pwd with garlic! Better vada paos are available. This place has lost its charm and is surviving on history, and not authentic anymore. Will never visit again. Sorry Bhau!

featured_reviews.name: Noel Nadar
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a famous place for Vada Pav in Ghatkopar. The size of the vada pav is very big, definitely tastes good and is worth the price charged for it. There's a little place inside to stand and eat. There are 2-3 chutneys kept there too. Even the misal pav here is great. It's located just outside Ghatkopar station. You definitely gotta visit this place if you're here and like vada pav!

featured_reviews.name: Fitfoodie Guy
featured_reviews.review_text: Good taste.. and a big vadapav makes once belly full.. also if someone is not that hungry you can share among two people.. additional we get groundnut chutney and onion..
